analysis:
Integration pass over all 30 units: docs and changelog, the selected-model recovery feature, shutdown unload bounding, daemon-state additions and tests. No concrete security regression found.

Checked against the replayed source: ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift:207 now also cancels the recovery attempt when a hold begins. That tightens the TB-012/T-059 load fence. The docs say recovery is refused or deferred under a hold, and the load path's addonHoldLoadRefusal is still described as unchanged. ProviderLoop+Autopilot.swift:213 only queues unloaded selected models for retry. The recovery loop (ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift) uses allowEviction:false and evicts only idle, unselected, unprotected, unheld models, after the Autopilot victim rules and a recheck just before each unload. It goes through ensureModelLoaded, so the hash, self-test, retirement and hold gates should apply. The makeAllDue calls after unload are scheduling hints only. Bounded backoff limits churn, which is an A-018, T-029 and T-016 availability question. The new adoption-release policy is flagged 'pending owner review'. It narrows what is served and does not widen routing or alter consent, App Attest or attestation (TB-011).

Shutdown (ProviderLoop+StartupShutdown.swift) now waits at most 15 s per model unload. A model whose native retirement never finishes is abandoned to process exit. T-028 residual GPU data is cleared at process exit, so no regression.

Daemon state gains enabledModelsAtStart, enabledModelsAtLastSwitch and selectedModelRecovery. They carry model IDs, timings and a blocker string; no keys, prompts or tokens. The decode paths are optional, so older state files still load. The test-only setters and seams are not a production surface.

Residual uncertainties, since this pass replayed only part of the source (omitted 168 units, complete=false): I could not see the recovery implementation or the unloadAllModelsForShutdown bodies. I could not confirm that recovery always routes through the hold and drain fences, or that a late recovery load cannot slip in after shutdown. TB-012/T-059 text may deserve a mention of recovery as a load initiator. needs_deeper_review is set for those unverified contracts, not for any observed flaw.
